data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Nidh' meaning 'night'. The name Nithi holds the grace and beauty of the night sky and the stars. In Hindu mythology, Nithi is considered a divine name associated with the goddess of night, Lakshmi. The name Nithi carries the meaning “Night, Star” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nithi usually hope their child will grow to embody night, star and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nithi carries a rich cultural significance in the Hindu tradition. In times of ancient India, evening rituals and rituals associated with nights were considered very important. Worship of various deities associated with night and stars was widespread. The name Nithi symbolizes the connection between humans and the cosmos and invokes a sense of tranquility, mystery, and the unknown.
data.spiritual_significance: Nithi is a spiritually significant name in Hinduism, symbolizing the goddess of the night and stars. Devotion to the night and stars was a common practice in ancient India, and the name Nithi deeply embodies this tradition. It is also believed that offering prayers to the deities associated with the night can bring peace, prosperity, and happiness. In addition, the name Nithi is considered auspicious and can bestow longevity, good health, and success in various aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nithi means 'the eternal divine consciousness' or 'the embodiment of eternal truth'. It symbolizes the inner wisdom and purity, guiding one towards the path of dharma and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Nithi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Nithya' meaning eternal or constant. The name Nithi carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Refers to the concept of eternal and unchanging truth or reality in Hindu philosophy.
